title: From Yellow‑Green Flicker to Nobel Blue LED

segments.text: Did a yellow‑green glow start LEDs?
In 1906 Henry Round saw silicon‑carbide crystals emit yellow‑green light under voltage.
Oleg Losev built the first silicon‑carbide LED in 1927.
Texas Instruments patented efficient near‑infrared gallium‑arsenide LEDs in 1962, proving reliable light emission.
In the early 1990s Shuji Nakamura, Hiroshi Amano, and Isamu Akasaki created the first practical blue LEDs.
Their blue chips enabled white light creation.
The trio received the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics for that breakthrough.
That Nobel‑winning blue chip opened the path to modern lighting.
